insights: Doubling the outer Napoleon construction = half-turn about the centroid: T_out²(z)ₖ = 2g − T_out(z)ₖ (the point-reflection law). This is the structural core; the orbit is a period-two cycle.

Half-turn equivariance napCenter(2g−b,2g−c)=2g−napCenter(b,c) is a PURE RING identity — the displacement coefficient cancels, so the period-two phenomenon is constant-free; a²=-1/12 enters only to first identify T_out² as the half-turn.
Proving T_out³=T_out compositionally (equivariance + reflection law) avoids the degree-4 polynomial identity that brute-force triple-composition expansion would require.
